title: UNICEF: 300 Children Killed in Gaza in 300 Days of 'Ceasefire' — Average of One Per Day
detail: UNICEF said in a statement on Thursday, August 6, 2026 that at least 300 children have been killed in Gaza in the roughly 300 days since the October 10, 2025 ceasefire was announced — an average of one child killed every day. UNICEF regional director for the Middle East and North Africa, Edouard Beigbeder, said "A ceasefire that leaves an average of one child dead each and every day is failing children." Hundreds more children have been wounded, many severely. UNICEF said families remain confined to about a third of the Gaza Strip, sheltering among destroyed buildings and rubble, with children continuing to face acute malnutrition, disease, unsafe water, and damaged sanitation; a shortage of incubators has left some premature newborns sharing machines. The statement was issued as UNICEF pressed parties to the proposed US-led Board of Peace plan to translate pledges into action.

media.caption: UNICEF says one child a day has been killed in Gaza since the October 2025 ceasefire

title: Eight Arab and Muslim Nations Jointly Denounce Ongoing Israeli Violations in Gaza
detail: Foreign ministers of the UAE, Qatar, Jordan, Indonesia, Pakistan, Turkey, Saudi Arabia, and Egypt issued a joint statement on August 6, 2026 expressing their "strongest condemnation and denunciation" of ongoing Israeli violations in Gaza, reserving particular criticism for the targeting of healthcare facilities and medical infrastructure alongside attacks on civilian areas and the continued killing of Palestinians, including women and children. The ministers said deliberate targeting of hospitals, ambulances, and medical personnel amounted to a "grave" breach of international humanitarian law, warning the continued attacks undermine international and regional efforts to implement the second phase of the plan to end the Gaza conflict following Hamas's acceptance of the Board of Peace roadmap. The statement followed an August 1 Israeli strike on a pharmaceuticals warehouse at al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital in Deir el-Balah; Gaza's Health Ministry said medicine shortages for cancer and blood-disorder treatment had reached 61%, with only about half of Gaza's 36 hospitals partially functional.

media.caption: Eight Arab and Muslim nations condemn Israeli violations in Gaza, citing attacks on healthcare facilities

title: Uganda's Parliament Approves Troop Deployment to Gaza Stabilization Force
detail: Uganda's parliament approved a government motion on Thursday, August 6, 2026 to deploy Uganda Peoples' Defence Forces (UPDF) troops to Gaza as part of the US-proposed International Stabilization Force (ISF), which is envisioned to grow to roughly 20,000 troops under American Maj. Gen. Jasper Jeffers. Ugandan Defense Minister Kiryowa Kiwanuka told lawmakers that President Trump, through emissaries, asked President Yoweri Museveni in July to consider contributing troops, citing Uganda's peacekeeping experience in Somalia. Uganda joins Morocco, Kazakhstan, Kosovo, Indonesia, and Albania in pledging soldiers for the ISF. Opposition lawmaker Hassan Kirumira questioned the deployment, asking "On which side is our army going to fight?" given Uganda's membership in the Organization of Islamic Cooperation. Kiwanuka said a status-of-forces agreement would be signed before any troops deploy; the ISF is not expected to enter Gaza until Israel completes a phased withdrawal under the ceasefire framework, which remains stalled over Hamas disarmament.

media.caption: International Stabilization Force troops are expected to deploy to Gaza after an Israeli withdrawal is completed
